text:
Toronto's November has turned into a referendum. The Maple Leafs are winless in four, outscored 17-7, and this is not a bad-luck story: they have had 42% of the expected goals in that run, the measure of who got the better chances. Auston Matthews drew headlines this week for calling out his teammates after the loss to the Devils, and the columns about his trade value have already started. Our playoff race puts Toronto's chances at 7%, with 18 points from 20 games. Twenty games is not a season, but it is long enough that the noise around this team is about more than a bad week.

Then there is the net. Sergei Bobrovsky is 0-5-0 over his last five starts with an .857 save percentage, 4.6 goals worse than the shots deserved. At the other end stands Jesper Wallstedt, the league's leader in wins and saves according to the Wild's postgame notes, at .924 and 15.9 goals saved above expected. He stopped 2.6 more goals than expected in Tuesday's overtime win in Montreal, a night The Athletic's Michael Russo wrote drew Carey Price comparisons.

Minnesota has points in nine straight (7-0-2) and 53% of the five-on-five expected goals this season. Kirill Kaprizov leads the league with 16 goals and has points in nine straight. Quinn Hughes has been the off-ice headline, topping Daily Faceoff's list of 2027 free agents, and Minnesota's power play (0.92 expected goals a game) meets a Toronto team taking 4.3 penalties a night.

The Leafs are without Kirill Marchenko (lower body) and Colton Sissons. John Tavares moved up beside William Nylander, Jack Roslovic took Marchenko's spot on the top power play and has 14 points in his last ten, and rookie Gavin McKenna is up to 15 minutes a night. Morgan Rielly is day-to-day and could return. Our Sleeper is Wild third-liner Bobby Brink, with 2.9 expected goals in his last ten games; we give him an 18% chance to score. Our numbers have Minnesota at 3.46 expected goals to Toronto's 2.73.
headline: The Leafs' slide meets the Wild's best goalie
